summary: The proposal addresses a relevant and well-motivated research topic (integrating Artemis with GitLab CI) and contains coherent content in its Problem Statement, Related Work, and Proposed Solution sections. However, it has fundamental structural deficiencies: three required sections (Introduction, Motivation, Objective) are entirely missing, the AI Transparency Statement is absent, the sole figure is a prohibited sequence diagram, the bibliography falls short of the minimum, and the schedule violates multiple agile-structuring rules (no 2-4 week iterations, forbidden writing/documentation items, horizontal layering). Additionally, pervasive writing issues (forbidden sentence starters, passive voice, filler words, first-person 'I') require systematic revision. Substantial restructuring and rewriting are needed before this proposal can be submitted.

findings.title: Missing required section: Introduction
findings.description: The proposal does not contain a dedicated 'Introduction' section. The document transitions directly from the Abstract to '1 Problem Statement'. A separate Introduction section (less than one page) is required by the guidelines.

locations.quote: The document ends with the Abstract on page 1 and proceeds directly to **1 Problem Statement** on page 2, with no Introduction section in between.

findings.title: Missing required section: Motivation
findings.description: The proposal lacks a dedicated Motivation section, which must be at most 3/4 page and should be visionary, outlining why it is scientifically important to solve the problem. The only motivational content is a single sentence in the Abstract ('it is possible to reduce the effort required to maintain the servers...') and a brief mention in the Problem Statement. A standalone Motivation section must be added.

locations.quote: Particularly smaller universities might then not use Artemis. There is no separate Motivation section anywhere in the document.
it is possible to reduce the effort required to maintain the servers

findings.title: Missing required section: Objective (with subsections in action form)
findings.description: The proposal lacks a proper 'Objective' section as required by the guidelines. Section 5 'Expected Findings' is a single narrative block without: (a) a short introductory paragraph, (b) a bullet list of 3-4 high-level objectives in action form (e.g., 'Integrate...', 'Extend...', 'Implement...') fitting in one line each, or (c) a dedicated subsection for each objective (each at least two paragraphs long). The entire section consists of three undivided paragraphs with no hierarchical structure.

locations.quote: This research thesis deals with the question on how to connect Artemis with GitLab CI. We expect to use the bridge pattern, described by Gamma et al. in their book Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software, for dynamically choosing the implementation with GitLab CI during startup of the system [Gamma95].

On long term, we expect that more universities will use Artemis... In addition, universities will save time and money as they will need at least one less server. No subsections or bullet-point objectives are present.

findings.title: AI Transparency Statement is entirely missing
findings.description: The proposal does not contain an AI Transparency Statement. The guidelines require a specific, first-person statement naming the AI tools used, their purpose, the sections in which they were used, and a confirmation that the author has carefully checked all AI-generated text. None of these elements appear anywhere in the document.

locations.quote: No AI Transparency Statement appears in any section of the proposal.

findings.title: Only one figure present (minimum two required) and it is a prohibited sequence diagram
findings.description: The proposal contains only one figure (Figure 1 on page 4), while the guidelines require at least two. Furthermore, Figure 1 is a sequence diagram (showing two actors with numbered message arrows 1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 2.2, 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 between lifelines), which is explicitly prohibited. The student must replace it with an activity diagram or communication diagram and add a second figure (e.g., component diagram or class diagram). As-is, the proposal also lacks any suitable UML diagram.

findings.title: Schedule not structured in 2-4 week iterations and follows horizontal layering
findings.description: The schedule is organized as a month-by-month list with sporadic single-week tasks rather than clear 2-4 week iterations. It follows a horizontal layering pattern (infrastructure → connectivity → API → results → models) rather than delivering vertically integrated, end-to-end features per iteration. It also does not reference the high-level objectives or demonstrate progressive working software at the end of each iteration. The schedule should be restructured into 2-4 week sprints, each delivering a working increment mapped to the stated objectives.

findings.title: Excessive use of filler words and superlatives
findings.description: The document contains seven instances of filler/superlative words across six pages: 'additional' (×2), 'Furthermore' (×1), 'Additionally' (×1), 'also' (×1), 'very' (×1), and 'In addition' (×2). For a document of this length this density is excessive. Remove or replace each instance with a more precise expression.

findings.title: Excessive passive voice constructions
findings.description: At least six sentences use passive voice, hiding the agent. The guidelines require active voice with identifiable subjects. Key instances: 'the build plans must be updated manually', 'the base build plan is copied', 'the build plan is fetched', 'the lecture is split up', 'the API of Artemis might be extended'. Rewrite so the actor performs the action.

findings.title: Section 4 relies entirely on a 14-item numbered list instead of prose
findings.description: Section 4 (System Requirements and Top Level Design) consists of a 1-line introductory sentence, a 14-item numbered list (the 'Flow of events'), and a 1-line concluding sentence. The section contains no substantive prose paragraphs. The scenario steps should be recast as flowing prose describing the workflow, with perhaps a few key steps retained as a list. The introductory sentence should also be expanded to at least 5 lines describing the actors, systems, and purpose.

findings.title: Krusche et al. paragraph in Related Work exceeds 10-line limit
findings.description: The second paragraph of Section 3 (Related Work), beginning with 'In their paper Interactive Learning...', spans from page 2 into page 3 and totals approximately 12-14 rendered lines, exceeding the 10-line upper limit. It should be split into two paragraphs: one introducing the Krusche et al. contribution and the interactive learning concept, and a second describing the concrete multi-phase lecture structure.

into multiple iterations, each consisting of diferent phases [Krusche17]. First there is a theory phase, before the instructor shows an example to the students.
